pl-l2d25c3-d1e108.summary: States that angels and saints living with the Lord, confirmed so that they neither will nor can turn to evil, do not lack free choice.

pl-l2d25c3-d1e111.summary: Cites Augustine, De civitate Dei XXII: as the first immortality lost by Adam was the ability not to die, so the first free choice was the ability not to sin, the last the inability to sin.
claims: The first freedom was able not to sin; the last unable to sin.

pl-l2d25c3-d1e114.summary: Cites the Enchiridion: man first had to be made able to will good and evil; later he will be unable to will evil, without thereby lacking free choice.
claims: Inability to will evil does not remove free choice.

pl-l2d25c3.summary: Holds that angels and saints confirmed in beatitude, who neither will nor can turn to evil, do not lack free choice. Augustine: as the first immortality was the ability not to die, so the first free choice was the ability not to sin, the last the inability to sin; man was first made able to will good and evil, but later will be unable to will evil, without losing free choice.
claims: Confirmed angels and saints have free choice though they cannot sin.
The first free choice was the ability not to sin; the last will be the inability to sin.
Inability to will evil does not remove free choice.
